On Fri, Jan 5, 2028 at 10:03 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Looping in Neha (Privacy & Security) and Karthik (Product) to provide the authoritative answers and evidence we can share.

Hi Claire — thanks for the checklist. Below is a concise Q&A you can cite; I added the specific timelines and what we can provide as evidence. If you need formal attestation language we can route through Legal.

Q: Do you use customer content to train models?
A: No. Redwood does not use customer-provided text, documents, or other content submitted via the Hosted API or Dedicated endpoints for model training, fine-tuning, or continual self-supervised updates to public models. This applies to: synchronous requests, asynchronous batch inputs, and content stored in request/response logs.

Q: Are there exceptions?
A: Only with explicit, contractually agreed opt-in where a customer provides data for a narrow-purpose fine-tune. That is a separate, auditable flow requiring a signed addendum and controlled access.

Retention (Hosted API):
- Request & response payloads: retained for 30 days by default for debugging & abuse prevention. Can be shortened via enterprise controls and retention policies.
- KV / prefix cache: ephemeral and scoped to instance lifetime; cache entries are not persisted to long-term storage in the hosted offering. Cache eviction occurs per TTL/batching policies (typically seconds–minutes).
- Operational logs (errors, infra traces): retained 90 days; aggregated metrics retained longer in anonymized form.

Retention (Dedicated capacity):
- Customers on Dedicated may configure retention windows. By default we keep request logs for 90 days unless the customer configures a shorter policy. On Dedicated we can also enable a 'no-logs' mode where request payloads are not sent to long-term stores; useful for high-sensitivity tenants.

Retention (Private / On-prem):
- For Private deployments, data residency and retention are controlled by the customer. Redwood's private package does not send customer content back to Redwood's hosted storage.

Deletion process and timelines:
- Immediate deletion: For hosted API, when a customer requests deletion of their account & data, we remove their primary records from active stores within 7 business days.
- Backup/DR snapshots: Persistent backups are purged on a 90-day cycle; we can accelerate purge of snapshots relating to a tenant and provide evidence of purge where required (see evidence below).
- Evidence & artifacts: We provide a deletion confirmation email plus an audit log extract (timestamped entries) and snapshot purge confirmations (hashes & purge job IDs). For enterprise accounts we can provide a signed deletion attestation.

Evidence packages we can share (attached / links):
- SOC2-2027-snapshot.pdf (controls overview and audit scope)
- Deletion playbook (we can export a time-stamped audit extract and purge job ids) — I attached a short text note with the playbook link.

Operational telemetry note:
- We collect aggregate telemetry (latency, RPS, error rates) to operate the service. These aggregates do not contain customer content and are retained for 24 months in anonymized form for product improvement and capacity planning.

If you need explicit wording for your Board memo, the sentence below is approved for inclusion (subject to Legal checkpoint):
"Redwood Inference does not train its public models on customer-provided content from the Hosted API or Dedicated capacity. Any use of customer content for model training requires an explicit, contractually-binding opt-in and an auditable process."

Karthik — small technical point on cache persistence / ephemeral behavior; please add if needed.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
